diagnostic_evidence.quote: N_{\eps}:= \sup_{\param_{0}\in \Param} \, \inf\, \{ n\ge 1 \,|\, \text{$\param_{n}$ is an $\eps$-approximate stationary point of $f$ over $\Param$} \}

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes a rate with constants depending on the initialization through at least f(param_0), the accumulated inexactness, and local Lipschitz constants on an initialization-dependent sublevel set. It supplies no uniform bound over param_0, although N_eps takes a supremum over all initializations. Indeed, for f(x)=x^2 on R and a fixed valid quadratic-gradient surrogate producing x_{n+1}=q x_n with 0<q<1, the required iteration count grows without bound as |x_0| grows, so the defined N_eps is infinite.

failure_location.quote: \item[(ii)] (Worst-case iteration complexity)  Suppose either  $r_{n}=1/( \sqrt{n} \log n)$ for $n\ge 1$ or $r_{n}\equiv \infty$. Then the worst-case iteration complexity $N_{\eps}$ for Algorithm \ref{algorithm:BMM-DR} satisfies $N_{\eps} = O(\eps^{-2} (\log \eps^{-1})^{2} )$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the worst-case definition or conclusion by a pointwise, initialization-dependent bound, or impose uniform bounds on the initial objective gap, inexactness, and smoothness constants over the allowed initializations.
issues.overall_effect: All advertised worst-case iteration-complexity conclusions under arbitrary initialization are unsupported; the proof yields only initialization-dependent complexity.
issues.title: Pointwise bounds do not imply the claimed worst-case complexity over arbitrary initialization
issues.why_classification: The least supported repair changes the central guarantee from a uniform worst-case complexity bound to an initialization-dependent one, or materially restricts the initialization regime.

issues.failure_explanation: At n=1, 1/(sqrt(n) log n) is undefined or infinite, so its squared sum cannot satisfy the assumed square-summability. In the no-radius branch, the asserted bound for every n>=1 has right-hand side zero at n=1, falsely forcing exact stationarity. The proof also chooses b_n=n^{-1/2}/log n from n=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a nonsingular sequence such as 1/(sqrt(n) log(n+1)), and state the logarithmic rate with an adjusted constant or only for sufficiently large n.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-n statement and the displayed trust-region choice are not valid as written, although the intended asymptotic order is unaffected.
issues.title: The stated logarithmic radius and rate are invalid at the first iteration
issues.why_classification: A local reindexing or logarithmic shift repairs the boundary case without changing the method, asymptotic rate, or substantive parameter regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $r_{n}\equiv \infty$, then surrogates  $g_{n}^{(i)}$ for all $n,i$ have $L_{g}$-Lipschitz contiuous gradients  for some constant $L_{g}>0$ and are $\lambda$-strongly convex

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption A3(b) gives only a lower bound on h_n relative to the current base point; it does not state or imply that g_n is strongly convex. For example, on a compact interval one can take f(x)=-rho x^2/2, base point zero, and h(x)=rho x^2/2, giving the convex but constant surrogate g=0. Distinct exact minimizers then have zero objective gap while remaining a positive distance apart, contradicting the proposition's conclusion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the strong-convexity condition from A5(b), or an equivalent error-bound condition, to the no-radius branch of the proposition.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition is false under its stated A1--A4 hypotheses. Its no-radius argument is valid only when the separate strong-convexity assumption is available.
issues.title: Asymptotic exactness incorrectly assumes strong convexity from the gap lower bound
issues.why_classification: The later asymptotic theorem already assumes A5, so adding the missing hypothesis locally repairs this proposition without weakening that theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: The crossing argument proves divergence of the sum of actual step lengths ||param_{n+1}-param_n||, while Proposition stationary_conditions requires divergence of the exact-minimizer displacements ||param_n-param_{n+1}^star|| or its separate normalized-gradient condition. Mere o(1) distance between exact and inexact iterates does not transfer divergence of these length sums. Summable objective-value gaps provide no such distance control for convex surrogates that are not strongly convex.

failure_location.quote: Then by Proposition \ref{prop:stationary_conditions}, there exists a  subsequence $(s_{k})_{k\ge 1}$ of $(t_{k})_{k\ge 1}$ such that $\param_{\infty}':=\lim_{k\rightarrow \infty} \param_{s_{k}}$ exists and is a stationary of $f$ over $\Param$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must derive quantitative distance control between each inexact update and an exact minimizer, or replace the crossing argument with one that works directly with actual inexact steps.
issues.overall_effect: The asymptotic-stationarity guarantee for inexact trust-region BMM is unproved. Exact trust-region executions are not affected by this particular mismatch.
issues.title: The inexact trust-region stationarity proof substitutes actual steps for exact-minimizer steps
issues.why_classification: Repairing the claimed robustness to merely summable optimality gaps requires a new error-control argument or stronger inexactness assumptions, rather than a local correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By collecting the columns $j=1,\dots, N$, it follows that $H_{n+1}$ in \eqref{eq:MUPR_NMF} is the global minimizer of $g_{n}$ over $\R_{\ge 0}^{r\times N}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The W-thresholding line reads from the undefined variable tilde W_n instead of W_n. More substantively, the W update multiplies by W_n rather than the thresholded tilde W_n, unlike the minimizer formula derived for the H block and the claimed symmetric construction. It also uses H_n rather than the freshly updated H_{n+1} required by the stated cyclic BMM scheme. For example, W_0=0 makes the displayed W update keep W_n=0 forever, even when X and H are positive and W=0 is nonstationary.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the W update using a defined thresholded W variable and the correct cyclic block data, then rederive both block updates from consistently centered surrogates and verify their exact-minimizer property.
issues.overall_effect: The executable MUR formula is not the BMM instance analyzed by the surrogate argument, so its convergence, stationarity, and complexity guarantees do not follow.
issues.title: The displayed MUR update is not the minimizer of the surrogate used to justify it
issues.why_classification: The intended symmetric update is discernible, but several coordinated algorithmic corrections and a renewed surrogate verification are required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, the sub-level sets $f^{-1}(( -\infty, a])=\{ \param\in \Param\,:\, f(\param)\le a \}$ for $a\in \R$ are compact.
\min _{W \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{p \times r}, H \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{r\times N}} f(W, H):=\frac{1}{2}\|X-W H\|_F^2

issues.failure_explanation: NMF sublevel sets on the full nonnegative orthant are not compact. For instance, W=0 gives the same finite objective value ||X||_F^2/2 for every nonnegative H, and the scaling transformation (W,H) to (cW,H/c) also preserves WH while becoming unbounded. Thus A2 does not hold trivially, and the boundedness and uniform surrogate-smoothness arguments used to invoke the main theorem are unavailable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, impose compact normalization constraints on the factors or prove an algorithm-specific boundedness theorem that controls the NMF scaling degeneracy.
issues.overall_effect: All three convergence and complexity conclusions for MUR lack the compactness hypothesis on which the cited theorem and the proof of bounded surrogate Hessians depend.
issues.title: NMF does not satisfy the compact-sublevel assumption claimed in the corollary
issues.why_classification: The direct supported repair materially changes the unconstrained nonnegative-factor regime, while no replacement boundedness argument is provided.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, the sub-level sets $f^{-1}(( -\infty, a])=\{ \param\in \Param\,:\, f(\param)\le a \}$ for $a\in \R$ are compact.

issues.failure_explanation: For CP factorization, multiplying one factor column by c and another by 1/c leaves every represented rank-one tensor unchanged. Hence sublevel sets are generally unbounded for both NCPD and unconstrained/general convex factor sets. The corollary invokes Theorem complexity without ensuring its compact-sublevel assumption.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for each compact subset $\Param_{0}\subseteq \Param$, there exist a constant $L_{f}=L_{f}(\Param_{0})$ such that $\lVert \nabla f(x) - \nabla f(y) \rVert\le L_{f} \lVert x-y \rVert$
The function $g_{n}^{(i)}$ in \eqref{eq:BProxLinear} is indeed a majorizing surrogate of $f_{n}^{(i)}$ when the objective $f$ has $L$-Lipschitz gradient and $\lambda \ge L$.

issues.failure_explanation: A2 provides only Lipschitz gradients on compact sets, whereas the prox-linear model is a global majorizer on an unbounded block only under a suitable global Lipschitz constant. There need not be any fixed positive stepsize that works from arbitrary initialization. For example, f(x)=x^4 is coercive and satisfies A2, but fixed-step gradient descent x_{n+1}=x_n-4x_n^3/lambda diverges from sufficiently large |x_0|.

failure_location.quote: Suppose \ref{assumption:A1} and \ref{assumption:A2} hold, where the convex constraint sets $\Theta^{(i)}$ are not necessarily bounded. issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume a global blockwise Lipschitz-gradient constant and choose lambda at least that constant, or replace the fixed step by a proved line-search or adaptive majorization rule.
issues.overall_effect: The BPGD convergence and complexity guarantee does not follow for the locally smooth coercive objectives and unbounded constraints allowed by the corollary.
